files: docs/migration/W6-记录与统计读接口迁移记录.md

discoveryCases.principle: Discover only the seven current role basenames and their timestamp/UUID rotated form; ignore unrelated files and directories.
Process rotated files before current files, then use lexical path order within each kind so rotation handoff drains old bytes first.
Directory discovery is bounded per poll and resumes after the saved lookahead entry so files outside one window are eventually observed without duplicates.

cursorCases.principle: A previously unseen current file starts at its observed EOF so enabling the importer does not replay an arbitrary historical current file.
A previously unseen rotated file starts at byte zero because it is immutable backlog that must be drained before deletion.
When identity is unchanged and file size grows, resume from the committed byte offset and line number.
If the same file identity shrinks below either committed offset or prior size, reset offset and line number and increment generation before reading new bytes.
When a file moves to a rotated path with the same identity, reuse its cursor and update only the path so the unread tail is not replayed or skipped.
When a path now points to a new identity, preserve the old identity cursor under an identity key and create a generation-zero cursor for the replacement.
A failed batch leaves the cursor at the last committed batch and records an error; the file remains pending and protected from rotation cleanup.
A rotated file is complete only when cursor offset reaches file size and no cursor error remains.

lineCases.principle: Generation zero preserves the legacy identity:offset source key so upgrades do not duplicate existing indexed rows.
After truncation, include generation in identity:generation:offset so replacement bytes at a reused offset receive a distinct stable ID.
Commit only complete newline-terminated lines; retain an unfinished tail in memory for the poll and do not advance the durable cursor past it.
Treat LF as the record delimiter and remove one trailing CR before parsing while byte offsets still include both delimiter bytes.
A whitespace-only complete line advances offset and line number but creates no runtime_logs row or facet count.
An invalid complete JSON line remains searchable as a warn parse-failure row with its raw text, file, byte offset, and line number.
Bound stored raw_json to 128 KiB without splitting UTF-8 and append a truncation marker inside the same budget; parsed summary metadata remains available.

timestampCases.principle: Normalize accepted offset, RFC1123, and canonical timestamps to UTC with millisecond precision before text-column ordering and facet comparison.
When time and createdAt are invalid or missing for one row, use one injected current UTC timestamp for both fields.

replayCases.principle: Replaying the same stable row ID inserts no duplicate and increments no facet a second time.
If row or facet persistence fails, keep the durable cursor at the last successful batch boundary so every uncommitted line is retried.

facetCases.principle: Update summary, normalized level, and nonblank event facets in the same transaction only for newly inserted rows inside the retention window.
Delete a bounded oldest batch and atomically decrement facet counts, remove zero buckets, and recompute earliest/latest retained times.

rotationRetentionCases.principle: File retention must not delete a rotated file while its cursor is short of size or has an error.
Cursor retention may remove only old cursors that reached file size and have no error; the physical rotated file uses its separate file-retention policy.
On rename plus replacement, drain the old identity at the rotated path before observing the new current identity so no tail crosses identities.

indexEnabledCases.principle: When the deployment index switch is enabled, the single owner performs bounded discovery/import and bounded index/cursor retention.
Disabling the index does not disable log files or grep; it disables directory scanning, cursor writes, row/facet writes, and index retention jobs.
When indexing is disabled, preserve historical rows/cursors/facets while removing importer protection so ordinary expired-file rotation cleanup can proceed.

nodeDefects.observed: W6 documents a 128 KiB raw_json limit, but normalizeRuntimeLogIndexInput stores input.rawJson unchanged and runtime-log-file-import-source-regression requires a greater-than-1-MiB raw_json to remain untruncated.
nodeDefects.goRule: Enforce the 131072-byte UTF-8-safe bounded representation before PostgreSQL write and retain summary/source metadata. Do not copy the unbounded Node behavior.

nodeDefects.observed: Node commits rows/facets in createRuntimeLogsBatchAsync and persists the file cursor in a later database operation, leaving a crash/rejection window that requires replay deduplication.
nodeDefects.goRule: Write new rows, facet deltas, and the cursor checkpoint in one PostgreSQL transaction; retain deterministic IDs as defense-in-depth replay protection.

goRecommendations.decision: Keep one production writer and additionally hold a PostgreSQL advisory lock or equivalent lease so accidental duplicate Go workers cannot consume the same spool concurrently.
Use a bounded bufio.Reader loop with explicit byte/line budgets and a reusable scratch/spill strategy; do not emulate Node stream chunk arrays or event-loop yields.
Commit rows, insert-only facet deltas, and cursor state atomically per bounded batch, with deterministic IDs for replay after ambiguous client failures.
Use bounded ordered PostgreSQL cleanup with row locking and SKIP LOCKED where concurrent maintenance is possible, then update facets in the same transaction.
